$comment: Data only. Each rule is one v1 fingerprint: a pattern v1-trained recall tends to write. 'silent' = it compiles/imports under v2 and fails only at runtime or only for modern-era clients. Code rules apply only to files that import the MCP SDK (see 'markers'), unless a rule sets anyFile. Every rule carries a 'bad' and 'good' example; `node check_v2.mjs --self-test` proves each pattern matches its bad and misses its good. Precision is checked against real v2 code too (reference/maintenance.md). Add a rule = add an object here; no code change.

rules.says: imports the v1 single package @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
rules.fix: import from '@modelcontextprotocol/server' (servers) or '@modelcontextprotocol/client' (clients)

rules.says: deep file import path; v2 packages expose only their exports map
rules.fix: import from the package root, or the '/stdio' subpath for stdio

rules.says: server.connect(new StdioServerTransport()) compiles under v2 but serves only legacy-era (2025) clients; modern clients fail to negotiate
rules.fix: serveStdio(() => createServer(deps)) from '@modelcontextprotocol/server/stdio'

rules.says: a hand-wired Streamable HTTP transport serves only legacy-era clients and drags in sessions
rules.fix: const handler = createMcpHandler(() => createServer(deps)); mount with toNodeHandler(handler) or export default handler
rules.bad: const transport = new NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined });

rules.says: session state; spec 2026-07-28 removed sessions, so this state is invisible to modern clients
rules.fix: keep state in explicit handles returned by a tool and passed back as arguments, or in signed requestState for multi-round calls

rules.says: variadic .tool()/.prompt()/.resource() were removed
rules.fix: server.registerTool(name, { description, inputSchema: z.object({...}) }, handler) — same for registerPrompt / registerResource
rules.bad: server.tool('greet', 'Greet a user', { name: z.string() }, async ({ name }) => ({ content: [] }));
rules.good: server.registerTool('greet', { description: 'Greet a user', inputSchema: z.object({ name: z.string() }) }, handler);

rules.says: raw Zod shape; accepted only by a deprecated overload that wraps it with the SDK's bundled Zod
rules.fix: inputSchema: z.object({ ... }) with `import * as z from 'zod/v4'`

rules.says: root 'zod' import while the project's manifest allows Zod < 4.2 (or declares no zod); v2 needs Zod >= 4.2 and fails at the first tools/list otherwise
rules.fix: import * as z from 'zod/v4' and depend on zod ^4.2

rules.says: v1 handler 'extra' object; v2 passes a structured ctx
rules.fix: ctx.mcpReq.signal / ctx.mcpReq.id / ctx.mcpReq._meta / ctx.http?.authInfo / ctx.http?.req

rules.says: server-to-client push request; throws on 2026-07-28 requests (MRTR replaces it)
rules.fix: return inputRequired({ inputRequests: { key: inputRequired.elicit({...}) } }) and read answers with acceptedContent()
rules.bad: const answer = await ctx.mcpReq.elicitInput({ message: 'Confirm?', requestedSchema });

rules.says: protocol logging is deprecated (SEP-2577); modern requests only receive it when they carry a logLevel
rules.fix: log to stderr (console.error) or OpenTelemetry; keep ctx.mcpReq.log only if clients rely on it

rules.says: -32042 must not be emitted on 2026-07-28
rules.fix: return inputRequired({ inputRequests: { login: inputRequired.elicitUrl({...}) } })
rules.bad: throw new UrlElicitationRequiredError([{ mode: 'url', url, message }]);
rules.good: return inputRequired({ inputRequests: { login: inputRequired.elicitUrl({ message, url }) } });

rules.says: v1 error class / enum
rules.fix: tools: return { content, isError: true }; resources/prompts: throw new ProtocolError(ProtocolErrorCode.InvalidParams, msg) or ResourceNotFoundError

rules.says: HTTP+SSE transport / frozen v1 copy; deprecated, removed in SDK v3
rules.fix: createMcpHandler(factory) over Streamable HTTP

rules.says: low-level handler keyed by a Zod schema constant
rules.fix: use McpServer.registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt; low-level handlers take method strings ('tools/call')
rules.good: server.registerTool('search', { description: 'Search', inputSchema: z.object({ q: z.string() }) }, handler);

rules.says: 2025-11-25 experimental tasks; removed from core in 2026-07-28 (now the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension)
rules.fix: drop it; long work returns a handle the model polls with a second tool

rules.says: stdout is the JSON-RPC channel on stdio; one console.log corrupts it
rules.fix: console.error(...)

rules.says: console.log in a file that serves both stdio and HTTP; harmless in the HTTP branch, corrupts the protocol in the stdio branch
rules.fix: console.error(...) — or confirm this line only runs in HTTP mode and add `mcp-v2-allow TS-STDOUT-LOG-MIXED`

rules.says: FastMCP was renamed; the module is gone in mcp 2.x
rules.fix: from mcp.server import MCPServer; from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context

rules.says: transport settings on the constructor raise TypeError in 2.x
rules.fix: mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", host=..., port=..., stateless_http=True) or mcp.streamable_http_app(...)

rules.says: mcp.settings holds no transport fields in 2.x
rules.fix: pass them to mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", ...)

rules.says: the second positional argument is now title, not instructions
rules.fix: MCPServer("name", instructions="...", version="1.0.0")

rules.says: protocol logging is deprecated (SEP-2577); modern requests only receive it when they carry a logLevel
rules.fix: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__); logger.info(...)  (goes to stderr)

rules.says: push-style server-to-client request; raises NoBackChannelError on 2026-07-28
rules.fix: a parameter Annotated[Model, Resolve(fn)] where fn returns Elicit(message, Model) (works in both eras)

rules.says: v1 error class McpError (2.x: MCPError(code, message, data); ErrorData itself still exists)
rules.fix: tools: raise ToolError(msg); protocol errors: raise MCPError(code, message) with `from mcp import MCPError`
rules.good: raise ToolError("No product with id 'x'. Use catalog_search_products to find ids.")

rules.says: camelCase attribute; 2.x types are snake_case (AttributeError at runtime)
rules.fix: .is_error / .structured_content / .input_schema / .output_schema / .next_cursor / .mime_type ...

rules.says: v1 context access
rules.fix: declare a `ctx: Context` (or Context[State]) parameter; ctx.mcp_server; ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
rules.good: async def tool(city: str, ctx: Context) -> str:

rules.says: v1 client helpers (and their 3-tuple)
rules.fix: async with Client("http://host/mcp") as client  — or Client(server) in tests

rules.says: low-level ClientSession + initialize (still supported in 2.x, the v1 shape); Client is the high-level form and negotiates the era
rules.fix: async with Client(target, mode=...) as client — target is a URL, StdioServerParameters, or an MCPServer
rules.bad: async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
rules.badFile:
from mcp import ClientSession
async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:

rules.says: module removed in 2.x
rules.fix: see reference/drift.md (Python table)

rules.says: HTTP+SSE transport; deprecated and not part of 2026-07-28
rules.fix: mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", stateless_http=True) or mcp.streamable_http_app(stateless_http=True)

rules.says: legacy-era clients get sticky sessions, so the endpoint cannot scale horizontally (modern clients are sessionless regardless)
rules.fix: pass stateless_http=True

rules.says: print() in a file that serves stdio; stdout is the JSON-RPC channel there
rules.fix: logging.getLogger(__name__).info(...) — logging writes to stderr
rules.badFile:
from mcp.server import MCPServer
mcp = MCPServer("x")
print("server ready")
mcp.run()

rules.says: -32002 (resource not found) and -32042 (URL elicitation) are not 2026-07-28 codes
rules.fix: resources: ResourceNotFoundError (TS) / MCPError(INVALID_PARAMS, ...) (-32602); URL flows: input_required

rules.says: includeContext values other than 'none' are deprecated
rules.fix: omit includeContext; call your LLM provider directly

project.says: TypeScript server code builds McpServer but nothing serves it through serveStdio or createMcpHandler, so no entry point speaks 2026-07-28
project.fix: local: serveStdio(() => createServer(deps)); remote: createMcpHandler(() => createServer(deps))

project.says: TypeScript tests connect a Client but never pin the modern era; the default Client speaks legacy, so the tests prove only 2025 behaviour
project.fix: new Client(info, { versionNegotiation: { mode: { pin: '2026-07-28' } } }) for the modern run (see templates/typescript/test/server.test.ts)

project.says: Python tests use Client but never mode="legacy"; most hosts still connect in the legacy era
project.fix: parametrize Client(server, mode=...) over "2026-07-28" and "legacy" (see templates/python/tests/test_server.py)

project.says: TypeScript >= 6 includes no @types packages unless tsconfig lists them; this project uses Node APIs but tsconfig has no "types", so `tsc` fails (TS2591) unless an imported package pulls Node's types in. A stdio-only server fails; with an HTTP adapter import it is a warning

A Resolve(...) resolver is defined inside a function in a module with `from __future__ import annotations`; the annotation stays a string the SDK cannot resolve, so MCPServer raises InvalidSignature when the tool is registered
project.fix: remove `from __future__ import annotations` from that module (Python >= 3.10 needs it for nothing here), or define the resolver at module level

project.says: The handler re-issues inputRequired whenever acceptedContent(...) is undefined, which is also the case after a decline or cancel: the user is asked again and again until the client gives up ("still required input after 10 rounds")
project.fix: ask only while inputResponse(ctx.mcpReq.inputResponses, key).kind === 'missing'; any answer other than an accepted yes returns a normal "did not" result (reference/typescript.md, Asking the user mid-call)

manifests.says: package.json depends on the v1 package @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
manifests.fix: depend on @modelcontextprotocol/server (+ /client, /node, /express as used); `npx @modelcontextprotocol/codemod@latest v1-to-v2 .` rewrites it

manifests.says: package.json depends on @modelcontextprotocol/server-legacy (frozen v1 copy, removed in v3)
zod range allows a version below 4.2; v2 converts schemas through Zod >= 4.2 and fails at the first tools/list otherwise
the mcp requirement targets v1 or has a v1-era floor without a <3 ceiling (e.g. mcp>=1.25 resolves to 2.x by accident)
httpx-sse is a v1-era dependency; mcp 2.x uses httpx2
manifests.fix: remove it unless your own code uses it

manifests.says: the mcp requirement has no version bounds; it resolves to 2.x today and will jump to 3.x on release
manifests.fix: "mcp[cli]>=2.3,<3" (a uv workspace member pinned by the workspace root can ignore this)
